newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Seita hit by new cancer suit.
newsitem.headline: France's Seita hit by new cancer suit.

text.p: The French tobacco giant Seita has been hit for the second time in a week by a lawsuit accusing it of causing a smoker's cancer, Seita and the lawyer for the smoker's family said Thursday.

The latest suit, only the second legal case of its kind brought in France, was filed in the southern city of Beziers by the family of a young woman who died of lung cancer last October after smoking Gauloises Brunes cigarettes for more than 20 years.
The suit said that Suzanne Berger of Servian, southern France, began smoking at the age of 13 and smoked 40 to 50 Brunes per day until she learned last year that she had cancer.
She had three children when she died a year after the initial diagnosis. She was 35.
The family's lawyer, Francis Caballero, said the suit was intended to force Seita to inform the public of the health risks of its products.

The suit, which accuses the tobacco maker of selling an "inherently dangerous" product due to its addictive properties and its link to cancer, seeks more than one million francs ($200,000) in damages and interest.

A Seita spokeswoman said the latest suit, like a similar complaint brought against the firm last week, lacked serious legal grounds. She said similar suits filed outside France had never led to damages payments of any kind in the past.
In the earlier suit, also prepared by lawyer Caballero, a two-pack-a-day Gauloise smoker who is near death accused Seita of causing his cancer.
